national law university and judicial academy, assam
Doctor of philosophy (Ph. D.)
PROGRAMME OBJECTIVES
1. To prepare legal researcher and scholars to understand and develop requisite legal research
acumen to critically examine legal theories, statutes and case laws.
2. To help legal researchers and scholars to explore their full potential to disseminate and
generate from established and contemporary theories the finer nuances of convergent and
divergent points and debates on multiple disciplinary discourses in contemporary time.
3. To generate human resources for research & development initiatives who are socially
relevant, practically sound and professionally competent researchers.
4. To prepare researcher and scholars to meet the challenges and opportunities which global
citizenry are offering to legal researchers and scholars in a globalized India.
PROGRAMME SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES
1. Fulfilling and executing the Ph.D. Course-work of the NLU, Assam for researchers and
scholars in orientation with the UGC research course work mandate.
2. Training researchers and scholars enrolled for the NLU. Assam Ph.D. Course-work to learn
the nitty-gritties of research and other related learnings thereto.
PROGRAMME learning outcome
1. Getting Ph.D. Course-workers oriented to the research universe.
2. Getting the Course-workers exposed to research in its nitty-gritty.
3. Getting them finetuned to research potential of major law subjects

Course
PHILOSOPHICAL FOUNDATION OF LAWS AND CURRENT TRENDS
Course Code: PHD 101PFL L T P 4 2 0 Credits: 6
Course Objectives
1. To introduce fundamental principles of Constitutional law critically
2. To understand principles of international law and their application into municipal law
3. To understand basic principles of criminal and tort law
4. To understand application of various principles while making law and policy.
Course Specific Outcome
1. After completion of course students will be able to
2. Students will be able to critically apply various principles of law
3. Students will be able to analysis the law on the basic principles of law.
4. Students will be able to think border area of law and their harmonisations.
SYLLABUS
Philosophy of Constitutional Law of India
Preamble, Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy and their inter se
relationship and Fundamental Duties.
Legal Theory
Concept of Law and Major Schools of Jurisprudence : Natural Laws School, Philosophical School,
Analytical School, Historical School and Sociological School.
International Law and Institutions
Nature of International Law and it’s relationship with Municipal Law, International Human Rights
Laws : UDHR, ICCPR, ICSECR, CEDAW, Convention relating to Rights of Disabled Persons.
Law of Torts & Crimes
General Principles of Criminal Law and Concept of Liability, Vicarious Liability and Absolute
Liability-Emerging trends in India .
Commercial Law
Essentials of a contract, Limited Liability Partnership and Role of Independent Directors, One Man
Company, CSR .

1. Pylee, M.V.; Indian Constitution; S. Chand Publication
2. Seervai, H.M; Constitution of India; Universal Publication
3. Jain, M.P; Indian Constitutional Law; LexisNexis

14. Treatise on Indian Partnership Act
15. Ratanlal and Dhirajlal; The Law of Torts; Universal Publication
16. Salmond and Heuston; The Law of Torts; Universal Publication
Course
LEGAL RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
Course Code: PHD 102LRM L T P 2 2 0 Credits: 4
Course Objectives
1. To familiarize researchers and scholars with the intricacies of legal research from varied
notions of legal theories and legal reasoning.
2. To introduce to researchers and scholars the idea of law from the perspective of the relation
of law and logic; competing idea of justice, experience and the also from the perspective of
the symbiotic relation between law and policy making.
3. To inculcate among researchers and scholars the quality being a critical legal researcher and
scholar who is incisive, confident, responsible and ethical.
Course Specific Outcome
1. On completion of the course researchers will be able be carry out independent doctrinal
research or empirical research.
2. Researchers and scholars are expected to be able to develop research problem, hypo-thesis
and research proposals to carry out qualitative research in multi-disciplinary dimensions.
3. Researchers and scholars will be equipped to prepare research design and also learn the what,
where and how of the tools and means to collect data for doctrinal research as well as field
research.
4. Researchers and scholars on the completion of the course will be able to test their hypothesis
and also engage in content analysis to eventually write report or thesis.
SYLLABUS
Legal Research and Methodology
Sources of Information, Identification and formulation of a research problem, Review of Literature,
Formulation of hypothesis, Research Design, Methods of Legal Research: doctrinal and non-
doctrinal research, Preparation of Synopsis, Rules of Interpretation.
Research Techniques
Data Collection: tools and techniques, Socio-metrics and Jurimetrics, Sampling Procedure: sample
design and sampling techniques, Survey and case study method, Scaling and Content Analysis, Use
of Questionnaires, Schedule & Interview, Legal material, Interpretations and Analyzing Data,
Statistical tools.
Decisional Materials including Foreign Decisions
Methods of discovering the “rule of the case”, Juristic writing-a survey of juristic literature it’s
relevance in selection of problems in India and foreign periodicals, Compilation of list of reports or
special studies conducted relevant to the problems, Formulation of the Research problem, Devising
tools and techniques for collection of data, Methods for the collection of statutory and case material
and juristic literature, Use of historical and comparative research material, Use of observation
studies, Use of questionnaires/interview, Use of case studies, Sampling procedures, Design of
sample, Types of sampling to be adopted, Use of scaling techniques.
Jurimetrics
Computerized Research-A study of legal research programs such as Lexis and West law coding,
Classification and Tabulation of data-use of cards for data collection, Rules for tabulation,
Explanation of tabulated data, Analysis of data-Qualitative and Quantitative, Report writing.
Selected: Research Funding Agencies and their guidelines .
Practical Exercises to be incorporated:
1. Report Writing
2. Synopsis Writing
3. Review of Literature
4. Case Study
Suggested Readings
1. Hugh Brayne, Nigel Duncan and Richard Grimes; Clinical Legal Education: Active
Learning inyour Law School; Blackstone Press
2. Agarwal, S. K.; Legal Education in India; N.M. Tripathi
3. Menon, N. P. Madhava; A Handbook of Clinical Legal Education, Eastern Book Company
4. William, J. Grade and Paul, K. Hatt; Methods in Social Research; McGraw Hil
Course
RESEARCH AND PUBLICATION ETHICS
Course Code: PHD 103RPE L T P 2 0 0 Credits: 2
Course Objectives
1. To enable the students to understand the basics of philosophy of research
2. To enable the students to understand research ethics
3. To develop research integrity
4. To develop publication ethics
Course Specific Outcome
At the end of course the students are able
1. To apply the research ethics in their research
2. To demonstrate ethical practices in research
3. To demonstrate research integrity
4. To produce high quality research
SYLLABUS
Philosophy and Ethics
Introduction to philosophy: nature and scope, concept, branches, Ethics: definition, moral
philosophy,nature of moral judgements and reactions.
Scientific Conduct
Ethics with respect to law and research, Intellectual honesty and research integrity; Publication
ethics: definition, introduction and importance, best practices/standards sittings initiatives and
guidelines; COPE, WANE etc. Conflicts of interest, scientific misconducts; Falsification,
Fabrication and Plagiarism (FFP), UGC Guidelines on Plagiarism and self-plagiarism, Redundant
Publications, Publication misconduct .
Publication Ethics
Publication ethics: definition, introduction and importance, Best practices/standards setting
initiatives and guidelines: COPE, WAME, etc. Conflicts of interest, Publication misconduct:
definition, concept, problems that lead to unethical behavior and vice versa, types, violation of
publication ethics, authorship and contributor-ship, identification of publication misconduct,
complaints and appeals, predatory publishers and journals, UGC Guidelines on Plagiarism and self -
plagiarism.
Practice: Open Access Publishing
Open access publications and initiatives, SHERPA/RoMEO online resource to check publisher
copyright and self-archiving policies, software tool to identify predatory publications developed by
SPPU, journal finder/journal suggestion tools viz. JANE, Elsevier Journal Finder, Springer Journal
Suggester, etc. Copyleft, Creative Commons Licences, Public Domain and Open Educational
Resources, reference tools.
Publication Misconduct
Group Discussions: Subject specific ethical issues, FFP, authorship, Conflicts of interest, complaints
and appeals: examples and fraud from India and abroad, Software tools: Use of plagiarism software
like Turnitin, Ouriginal and other open source software tools, Google originality check, Ouriginal
(Urkund has been changed to Ouriginal).
Databases and Research Metrics
Databases, Citation databases: Web of Science, Scopus etc. Research Metrics, Indexing and
Abstracting databases, Research Metrics: Author level, Article level and Journal level.
Suggested Readings
1. Hugh Brayne, Nigel Duncan and Richard Grimes; Clinical Legal Education: Active
Learning inyour Law School; Blackstone Press
2. Agarwal, S. K.; Legal Education in India; N.M. Tripathi
3. Menon, N. P. Madhava; A Handbook of Clinical Legal Education, Eastern Book Company .
4. William, J. Grade and Paul, K. Hatt; Methods in Social Research; McGraw Hill .
5. UGC notification regarding maintenance of Standards in Research and Ethical norm
